newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: U.S.'s Albright to visit Guatemala.
newsitem.headline: U.S.'s Albright to visit Guatemala.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright is scheduled to visit Guatemala on May 4 to observe the peace process and perform other duties, officials said on Monday.
She is also expected to help iron out details of a visit by President Bill Clinton on May 8 to Costa Rica for a meeting of Central American heads of state, officials said.

Albright will observe Guatemala's ongoing peace process with a visit to a guerrilla demobilization camp constructed in part with U.S. funds, a spokeswoman for the Guatemalan foreign relations minister said.
Ex-rebels have lived for three months in eight disarmament camps while they turn in weapons under terms of a December peace treaty that ended 36 years of civil war in Guatemala.
From Guatemala, Albright will continue to Mexico City to join Clinton, who is scheduled to spend May 5-7 there before heading to Costa Rica to attend the Central American summit.
With Central America's last internal armed conflict over in Guatemala, presidents from the isthmus hope to put trade and immigration issues at the top of the agenda for the summit.
